caveats: Each record is what the commission published. Findings, opinions and statements are quoted in the report's own words and carry the report's own label; OPAX does not summarise, grade or reword them.

Allegations are not findings. A commission's finding or opinion of corrupt conduct or misconduct is not a finding that a person is guilty of a criminal offence, and the commissions say so in their reports.

Commissions use different statutory terms (for example serious corrupt conduct in New South Wales, serious misconduct opinions in Western Australia). Do not compare counts across commissions as if the terms were the same.

A list marked not_extracted is unknown, not empty: the report may contain findings or recommendations that OPAX could not extract reliably (scanned pages, unusual layouts). stated_none means the report itself says there are none.
Bodies and public roles named in a report are recorded as the report names them. OPAX adds no names and does not create pages for private individuals.
Responses and implementation status appear only where the commission publishes them; their absence does not mean an agency did not respond.

bodies.name: National Anti-Corruption Commission
gaps: www.nacc.gov.au gave the identifying OPAXBot agent no response on 11 November 2026 (HTTP/1.1 timeouts, HTTP/2 stream resets), so its investigation reports and statements are not collected automatically.

Eight investigation reports are included from a manual publisher download supplied by the OPAX maintainer on 11 November 2026 (cited to their nacc.gov.au URLs). Later reports and NACC statements are not included.
webarchive.nla.gov.au answered the identifying agent with HTTP 403, so the official archive copy is not used either.

licence.note: Page 2 of each report licenses the material under CC BY 4.0, except the Commonwealth Coat of Arms, the Commission's logo, third-party material, trade marks and images.

bodies.name: Independent Commission Against Corruption
gaps: Reports on investigations made public before 2016 are not online: the ICAC keeps only a summary for each, and copies must be requested from the ICAC. Those records hold the ICAC's published summary; findings and recommendations are not extracted.
The ICAC copyright statement reserves all rights (fair dealing aside). OPAX keeps short verbatim finding and recommendation passages with links to the original report.

Findings are read from the summary chapter of each report PDF. Where a finding's particulars run past the cited page only the finding statement is kept, and reports whose layout could not be read confidently are marked not_extracted.
Agency action plans and progress reports are listed as documents; their contents (implementation status for each recommendation) are not parsed.
Report PDFs without a text layer (scanned images, for example Operation Scania) are not OCRed; their findings stay not_extracted.
Many pre-2016 summaries give only the month a report was made public; those records carry no date and a note with the month, because the schema holds day-level dates only.

licence.attribution: NSW Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC). ICAC materials are protected by copyright and all rights are reserved; OPAX keeps short verbatim passages with links to the original and the ICAC's copyright notice.

bodies.name: Independent Broad-based Anti-corruption Commission
gaps: www.ibac.vic.gov.au answered the identifying OPAXBot agent with HTTP 403 (CloudFront) on 11 November 2026, for its pages and its robots.txt. IBAC reports are read from the copies tabled in the Parliament of Victoria instead.
IBAC publications that are not tabled (research and prevention reports, recommendation-progress pages and agency responses published only on IBAC's site) are therefore not loaded.

Some tabled papers are listed by the Parliament without an online document (for example the Special report on Operation Sandon, available on request from the Parliament); their recommendations are not loaded.
Findings and opinions are not extracted; read each report for them.

licence.attribution: Independent Broad-based Anti-corruption Commission; tabled copy published by the Parliament of Victoria

bodies.name: Crime and Corruption Commission
gaps: Reports from 1991 to about 2011 are listed on the CCC site but many pages link no report document; those records carry the page summary only, with findings and recommendations not extracted.
Scanned reports without a text layer are not OCR'd; their findings and recommendations are not extracted.

Findings and opinions are not extracted except where a report states it makes no finding about any person (section 48B of the Crime and Corruption Act 2001). Pre-2025 reports state outcomes in narrative form, which is not converted into findings.
Recommendations are extracted only from a complete numbered run; reports that number recommendations differently, or set them inside narrative chapters only, are marked not_extracted.

Government responses are recorded where the CCC report or public hearing page links one; the responses themselves (often Queensland Parliament tabled papers or ministerial statements) are linked, not fetched.
The 1989 Fitzgerald Inquiry report, which the CCC hosts, is a commission of inquiry report and is not included here.

licence.note: The CCC copyright page licenses its website material under CC BY 4.0 unless otherwise noted; individual publications may carry their own copyright details.

bodies.name: Corruption and Crime Commission
gaps: The Commission's website has no copyright or licence page; reports carry the Commission's copyright notice (fair dealing only), so OPAX keeps short verbatim extracts with citations and links the original PDFs.
Only the reports listing (/publications/reports) is covered. Annual reports, quarterly reports filed under /quarterly-reports, media releases and news items are not report records.

The listing date is the date the Commission's page was created; the record date is the report's cover date or the tabling date stated on the page where one is given, and the listing date only as a fallback.

Opinions are extracted only where the Commission states them in a sentence on a single page; opinions in older reports framed differently, or split over a page break, are not extracted (findings not_extracted).
No text layer, no OCR: scanned reports have no extracted opinions or recommendations.

licence.attribution: Corruption and Crime Commission (Western Australia). Copyright in each report is held by the Commission; further use is limited to what the Copyright Act 1968 (Cth) permits. The website publishes no copyright or licence page.

bodies.name: Independent Commission Against Corruption (South Australia)
gaps: Office for Public Integrity: publishes only its annual reports (excluded); no OPI report or statement records.
Since October 2021 the Commission does not make findings of corrupt conduct; most records have no findings.
Government and agency responses are recorded only where the Commission's page links them or the report reproduces them; implementation status is not published by the Commission as structured data.
Scanned reports without a text layer are not read (no OCR); their recommendations stay not_extracted.
Recommendations are extracted only from numbered 'Recommendation N' lists; reports that set out recommendations in prose, tables or unnumbered lists keep recommendations_status not_extracted.
Findings are extracted only from investigation reports that state them in the Commissioner's own words (Oakden 2018, Gillman 2015); public statements are not read for findings.

licence.attribution: © Independent Commission Against Corruption SA. The site states copyright and grants no open licence; records quote and link the Commission's publications.

gaps: www.integrity.tas.gov.au (Cloudflare) answered the identifying OPAXBot client with HTTP 403 on 11 November 2026, so the Commission's reports are not collected automatically.

webarchive.nla.gov.au (the official archive) answered the identifying agent with HTTP 403, so archived copies are not used either.

licence.status: copyright (Integrity Commission); reuse under the Tasmanian Government terms

bodies.name: ACT Integrity Commission
gaps: Confidential reports given to a Legislative Assembly committee are not published; only the Commission's announcement of the Operation Kite confidential report is recorded.
The Commission does not publish numbered recommendations of its own in these reports; numbered recommendations quoted from the Auditor-General or the Public Accounts Committee are not recorded.
Ministerial responses to special reports are presented to the Legislative Assembly and are not on the Commission's site; they are not loaded.
The lobbying inquiry (open, with two discussion papers) has not reported; discussion papers are not reports.
Discontinued investigations are not published individually.

licence.terms: Copyright owned by the ACT Integrity Commission; material may be reproduced in unaltered form for personal, educational or non-commercial use with attribution (copyright page).
